page: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache, complemented by 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage, and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute and throughput capacity under parallel execution, alongside limitations in per-thread execution speed. The instance registers strong multi-core processing performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 81317.48 and a PassMark CPU score of 55855.44. In contrast, single-thread performance ranks in the lower tiers, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core rating of 1384.19 and modest single-threaded compression throughput. Memory subsystems deliver high throughput, surpassing 219 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and driving 74.14 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, CPU-based LLM generation benchmarks highlight low token throughput, demonstrating the inefficiency of running large model text generation on this architecture.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the r5b.24xlarge provides high memory and thread density, making it cost-efficient for consolidation of multi-threaded services that demand large working sets in RAM without requiring specialized accelerators. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and lagging single-core responsiveness. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, enterprise memory-intensive caching layers, Clang software builds, and multi-threaded batch operations.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores clocked at 3.1 GHz, paired with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding an 8.0 GB allocation per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned at 25 Gbps baseline, with no local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration included. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier parallel execution, achieving strong results in multi-core stress testing, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and large-block memory read bandwidth exceeding 219 GB/sec. It also exhibits high performance in in-memory workloads, sustaining 74.14 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core benchmarks and LLM generation metrics indicate below-average serial speed. The instance functions effectively for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis distributed caching, enterprise analytics, and high-concurrency multi-threaded workloads.
